test.name: Spec 0010 spike: spool as specified (O_RDONLY reader, f_bsize punch)

expected: a spool reader opened O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW can fcntl(F_PUNCHHOLE) ranges aligned to f_bsize from fstatfs, keeping allocation under 2 MiB under the AC-12 load, and lseek(SEEK_DATA) then gives the first unreleased data (spec 0010 AC-12, Adapter macOS row Spool, exactly as written)
actual: F_PUNCHHOLE on an O_RDONLY descriptor fails with EPERM; it works on O_RDWR. With f_bsize (4096 on this APFS volume) alignment the punch succeeds, but the block of a punched range that lies in the 16 KiB VM page the child is still appending to comes back as zero-filled allocated data: 4 MB appended with 40 punches left 233472 B allocated, SEEK_DATA pointed at 294912 (bytes there are zeros) instead of 3997696, and 37 of 40 SEEK_DATA answers were stale; fsync of writer or reader does not change it. Under the AC-12 load (fake at 2000 lines/s for 60 s, about 6 MB per stream, drained and punched every 500 ms through an O_RDWR reader) combined allocation reached 3272704 B and kept rising (t=15 s 2256896, t=60 s 3272704), SEEK_DATA after the run was 32768 while 6008832 bytes had been released, and resuming from SEEK_DATA read only zeros. The rest of the row works as written: create with O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC gives a 0600 file and EEXIST on a second create, O_NOFOLLOW refuses a symlink, SEEK_DATA is 0 on fresh data and ENXIO on an empty or fully punched file, punched ranges read back as zeros, st_size is unchanged, unaligned punches fail with EINVAL, the spool keeps growing after the spawning daemon died and a new daemon reads it from SEEK_DATA 0. The working variant is the next record (O_RDWR reader, page-size alignment).
